tracking_and_ingestion_systems.cv_pipeline_specs: Proposed dual-track design (10 Hz is the platform output target, not a guarantee of broadcast quality): decode each licensed broadcast at native frame rate; run sport/venue-specific YOLOv8 models for player, ball/puck, official and equipment; pass boxes, class confidence and timestamps to ByteTrack; and emit a canonical sample every 100 ms. Retain low-confidence candidate detections for association, since ByteTrack uses low-score boxes to recover occluded objects, while storing track confidence, missed-frame count, ID-switch count and lifecycle state. Identify surveyed field/court landmarks and solve a versioned perspective matrix; map player footpoints and ball/puck centers, rather than box centers, into sport coordinates. Use OpenCV getPerspectiveTransform/warpPerspective, camera-cut detection and interpolation only across short gaps; reject samples when reprojection error, blur, occlusion or homography residual exceeds threshold. Stitch views with venue-camera calibration and appearance/jersey re-identification, then reconcile CV tracks to official IDs using roster/lineup feeds. Publish frames/detections/tracks to Kafka keyed by game_id/entity_id; Flink performs event-time ordering, watermarking, deduplication, late correction and stateful joins; a materializer resamples to 10 Hz and stores native observations plus velocity, acceleration and spacing. Official tracking, where licensed, is primary truth; CV is fallback/quality control and is marked source=cv with uncertainty. Benchmark MOTA/IDF1, coordinate reprojection error, ball recall and end-to-end p95 latency by sport/camera before commercial enablement.

official_feed_integration.value: Sportradar adapter: contract for league-specific NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL and Soccer APIs; use authenticated server-side HTTPS REST retrieval plus documented real-time Push feeds, accept JSON/XML where offered, persist provider event/game/player IDs, and handle corrections by event revision. Sportradar describes its APIs as B2B and says they are not intended to be called directly from a client application. League pages document live scores, play-by-play/statistics and push capabilities; MLB additionally documents a separately permissioned Statcast package and NBA live event positional data. This is a design, not a claim that one subscription includes every product.

Genius Sports adapter: contract for official, low-latency live/historical data and play-by-play, then normalize the licensed delivery into the Event/Participant/Market schema. Genius markets official partner coverage, direct-from-stadium real-time data and odds APIs; verify league, territory, retention, analytics and downstream redistribution rights in the order form rather than assuming all five requested sports share identical coverage or protocol details.

Second Spectrum via Genius: use only a separately licensed feed or delivery channel for contracted competitions. Genius identifies Second Spectrum as official tracking provider for EPL, NBA and MLS and describes AI/computer-vision capture of precise ball/player locations and rapid action indexing; that announcement does not establish official Second Spectrum coverage for NFL, MLB or NHL. Keep raw tracking, calibration metadata, entity mapping and rights scope separate from the generic CV fallback.

Kalshi market adapter: if agreement permits, ingest quotes/trades through its documented API as a separately identified market source, not sports truth. Kalshi documents real-time market data/trade execution, API-key plus RSA-signature authentication, and token-based read/write rate limits. Never expose provider credentials to tenants and do not route orders unless contract, product design and applicable law expressly authorize it.

Target-site boundary: DraftKings, Action Network and BettingPros are product/market UX references, but their fetched terms do not authorize scraping or backend reuse. DraftKings terms prohibit bots, scripts, AI, parsers, spiders and screen scrapers; Action Network and BettingPros restrict retransmission, copying and commercial exploitation. Use only an expressly authorized API/affiliate/enterprise feed and attach provider entitlement to every response.

commercial_and_legal_framework.derived_data_strategy: Adopt a rights-first product boundary: raw provider payloads, live play-by-play, raw tracking coordinates, logos, photos, video, articles and near-live feeds are licensed assets or restricted content; they never enter a customer response unless entitlement explicitly permits it. Contract directly with Sportradar/Genius/Second Spectrum or the applicable league for commercial display, internal storage, model training, derivative/derived works, historical retention, territories, betting/fantasy use, attribution, audit, service levels and downstream redistribution. Build transformed analytics from permitted inputs—posterior probabilities, aggregated rates, model scores, feature vectors, matchup indices, alerts and simulation summaries—while minimizing row-level raw reconstruction and preserving provenance/transformation lineage. Do not rely on a generic facts-are-free theory: U.S. fair use is fact-specific, balances purpose/character (including commercial use), nature, amount and market effect, and has no safe percentage rule; contracts, database rights, trademarks, publicity, access controls and confidential rights can independently constrain use. NBA terms restrict commercial reproduction/use of basketball content and statistics, while MLB terms restrict distribution, modification, rebroadcast and derivative use of digital properties. Obtain counsel written clearance for each product and jurisdiction.
commercial_and_legal_framework.sub_licensing_compliance: Maintain a machine-readable rights matrix with provider, league/competition, sport, territory, customer class, fields, latency, historical window, retention/deletion, derived-work permission, display/redistribution/sublicensing permission, attribution, audit, security and termination. The commercial deal should say whether the platform may sublicense API responses, permit customer caching, train models, sell transformed analytics or share outputs with sportsbooks/media/fantasy operators; a derived-data label cannot cure a missing right. Keep raw licensed data in a restricted zone, tokenize provider IDs, attach rights_scope and expires_at to every feature/prediction, and enforce entitlements at query time. Add takedown/deletion workflows, audit logs, provider reconciliation and a kill switch. NBA/MLB terms show why public league websites cannot be treated as resale licenses; DraftKings terms show why automated collection is prohibited in the fetched jurisdiction; Action Network and BettingPros restrict commercial copying/retransmission. This is operational guidance, not legal advice.
commercial_and_legal_framework.api_distribution_architecture: Put a multi-tenant API gateway between customers and feeds. Authenticate customers with OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow (PKCE for public clients where applicable); authorization issues short-lived scoped tokens, and the gateway maps claims to tenant_id, plan, sport, competition, fields, latency and redistribution entitlements. Keep provider credentials in a server-side secrets manager; use vendor-specific signed-key authentication where required (Kalshi uses key ID, timestamp and RSA signature), not invented OAuth. Flow: adapters -> Kafka -> Flink live state -> Spark/Iceberg/Delta feature store -> model service -> entitlement-aware REST/GraphQL API/webhooks. Enforce per-tenant/global token buckets, concurrency limits, response-size caps, tenant-aware cache/dedup keys, provider backoff, Retry-After handling, 429 metrics, circuit breakers and a kill switch. Use row/column authorization, tenant-scoped encryption/audit logs, idempotency keys, no cross-tenant cache leakage, and separate read-only analytics from order execution. RFC 6749 defines OAuth limited-access authorization; RFC 6585 defines HTTP 429 and optional Retry-After; neither grants data rights.

data_lifecycle_2018_2025.historical_pbp_storage: 2018-2024 tier: land each licensed raw response immutably in object storage with checksum, provider, retrieval time, source timestamp, rights/schema version; normalize to append-only PBP/Event facts keyed by sport, season, competition, game_id, event_id, sequence, event_time, participants, state-before/state-after and correction metadata. Keep roster, venue, schedule, injury, odds and settlement dimensions separate, then publish columnar Iceberg or Delta tables partitioned by sport/season/game_date and clustered by game_id/event_time. Use deterministic IDs and idempotent merges for corrections; never overwrite a snapshot used by a released model. Iceberg metadata snapshots/atomic commits and schema/partition evolution, or Delta ACID/time travel and batch-stream unification, provide reproducible reads and audit rollback. Coverage is product-specific: Sportradar documents full NFL PBP, MLB pitch/event feeds and Statcast access beginning in 2020, NBA event/PBP, NHL PBP and Soccer real-time feeds, so availability and license scope must be recorded instead of assuming uniform 2018 coverage.
data_lifecycle_2018_2025.high_res_tracking_lakehouse: 2025+ tier: retain replayable source streams and native-rate observations in Kafka/object storage; key streams by stable game_id for partition ordering and deduplicate by provider_event_id plus observed_at/revision. Flink consumes event time with watermarks, keyed state and checkpoints, joins roster/lineup/PBP/injury context, handles out-of-order records and corrections, and emits a canonical 10 Hz table with game_id, entity_id, t_ms, x/y/optional z, coordinate system, source, camera/calibration version, confidence, interpolation flag, rights_scope and model_version. Keep raw CV frames/detections in a restricted short-retention zone and compact validated tracks/features into Iceberg/Delta tables partitioned by sport/season/game_date and clustered by game_id/entity_id; maintain a hot materialized view for live APIs and a cold lakehouse for replay. Do not infer that source cadence or tracking permission is identical across NFL/MLB/NBA/NHL/Soccer: store source_cadence_hz and licensed_coverage metadata and downsample only after preserving native observations. Kafka documents durable/replayable events and per-key order; Flink documents checkpointed exactly-once state recovery; Delta/Iceberg document ACID/snapshots/evolution.
data_lifecycle_2018_2025.backtesting_framework: Use Bayesian rolling-origin walk-forward backtesting. At forecast cutoff t, materialize only the Iceberg/Delta snapshot and odds/lineup/injury records available at t; fit/update hierarchical posterior, draw parameters and latent availability states, run the production simulation/prop engine, freeze model/data/config/seed IDs, and score after settlement/outcome becomes observable. Repeat through 2018-2025+ with season boundaries, expanding/sliding windows and sport/market strata. Report log score and Brier/calibration for probabilities, interval coverage and CRPS/quantile scores for distributions, residuals by venue/lineup/source, and betting metrics net of vig, pushes/voids, limits, line movement and execution. Add leakage tests for future corrections, postgame tracking, final lineups, injury timestamps and revisions; compare market-implied and simple baselines. PyMC/Stan posterior predictive checks and the cited soccer first-half-to-second-half out-of-sample design support this workflow; MC standard error, convergence diagnostics and reproducible seeds are release gates.

advanced_prop_modeling.correlation_logic: NFL joint prop model: Draw a latent state z=(pace, drives, pass rate, weather, score differential, opponent pressure, team total) and a lineup; generate snaps, routes, targets, carries, air yards, completions, sacks, scrambles and touchdowns conditionally. Compute P(all legs) from shared draws, not product of marginals; expose covariance, binary Pearson rho and conditional probabilities. QB passing yards, team win/total, receiving targets and opposing volume are linked through drives, pass rate and script; include pushes/voids.
advanced_prop_modeling.injury_impact_variables: Treat LT absence as a probabilistic protection state: replacement quality, pressure/sack hazard, time-to-throw, QB scramble/design rush, pass depth, run-block efficiency, RB share, play action, drive success and opponent edge matchup. Use LT_absent × opponent_edge × QB_mobility interactions; propagate status and snap uncertainty; shrink sparse effects toward position/unit means.

advanced_prop_modeling.correlation_logic: NBA joint prop model: Sample active lineup, rotation, minutes and pace; jointly allocate usage, assists, rebounds, threes, points, steals and blocks across possessions. Shared pace, spacing, assist opportunities and rebound pool create player-to-game and player-to-player dependence; usage competition can be negative. Price parlays from joint draws and exact five-man units, not independent marginals.
advanced_prop_modeling.injury_impact_variables: For each absence shift active/starter probability, minutes, substitutions, usage, touch time, rebounding/assist opportunity, defensive matchup, spacing and blowout probability; interact replacement role with opponent pace and back-to-back fatigue. Marginalize plausible rotations announced before tip and publish lineup IDs plus minutes/usage uncertainty.

advanced_prop_modeling.correlation_logic: MLB joint prop model: Simulate plate appearances in order, handedness, pitch mix/quality, park/weather, base-out state and bullpen state; derive hits, total bases, HR, RBI, runs and strikeouts from the same inning paths. PA opportunity links batter props; lineup position and team run environment link RBI/runs/hits; pitcher exit links opposing strikeouts and hitter outcomes. Use hierarchical rates with shrinkage and predictive intervals.
advanced_prop_modeling.injury_impact_variables: Model batter availability, lineup slot, expected PA, sprint/baserunning limitation, defensive replacement and platoon substitution; for pitchers model workload, pitch count/innings, velocity/spin/command and early-removal probability. Reallocate teammate run/RBI/PA when a hitter or starter is absent, with park, weather, handedness and opponent covariates; use age, position and past performance rather than last-game bumps.

advanced_prop_modeling.correlation_logic: NHL joint prop model: Simulate shifts/possessions with team strength, shot generation/prevention, manpower, zone, line matching and goalie state; jointly generate goals, shots, assists, saves, blocks, hits, faceoffs and time-on-ice. Power plays, score effects and goalie workload link legs; teammate points share goal events and opposing shots share goalie state. Use direct joint simulation for parlays.
advanced_prop_modeling.injury_impact_variables: Sample goalie start/save-rate uncertainty, skater availability, shifts/time-on-ice, line/pair assignment, special-teams role, replacement quality, matchup and rest/travel. Reallocate shots/goals/assists/blocks through unit-level latent strengths; a star defender absence changes goalie shot quality and teammate minutes rather than a single team-total delta.

advanced_prop_modeling.correlation_logic: Soccer joint prop model: Use dynamic attack/defense/venue state and a low-score-corrected bivariate goal model; simulate possession/shot/event paths for player props. Link shots, SOT, assists, goals, cards and minutes to common team-goal, possession and game-state draws; price result/total/forward legs as joint events. Explicitly model missing observations and validate by posterior predictive checks and out-of-sample forecasts.
advanced_prop_modeling.injury_impact_variables: Sample starter probability, minutes, role, set pieces, pressing/defensive workload, shot/assist rates, substitution hazard and formation. Shift opponent-specific attack/defense and team-goal rates when goalkeeper, defender, playmaker or striker is absent; treat reports as noisy timestamps and avoid identical fixed goal adjustments across competitions.

algorithms.value: Poisson/Dixon-Coles count engine: for soccer, low-scoring baseball runs, hockey goals and event counts use log(lambda_home)=alpha+attack_home-defense_away+venue+covariates and an analogous away rate, with negative-binomial alternatives for overdispersion. Add the Dixon-Coles low-score dependence correction and time-varying team strengths for soccer; for NFL/NBA prefer possession/drive/play point models instead of independent low-rate goals. Convert score distributions into win/draw/loss, totals and prop probabilities by summation or simulation.

Monte Carlo posterior-predictive engine: draw theta from the Bayesian posterior, lineup/injury/venue states from distributions and conditional game-event paths from sport-specific likelihoods; retain each draw as a coherent game so joint props and season outcomes are preserved. Estimate P(A)=M^-1 sum I(A_m), joint probabilities with I(all legs), and uncertainty with Monte Carlo standard errors; use reproducible seeds, convergence checks and scenario sweeps. The cited review emphasizes random sampling, reproducible pseudo-random sequences, cost and sensitivity to model/input quality.

Glicko-2 online rating layer: maintain each team/unit/player rating r, rating deviation RD and volatility sigma; update by rating period using outcomes, inflate uncertainty during inactivity, and expose rating plus uncertainty as a prior/feature to the richer Bayesian model. Use sport-specific periods and validate them—Glickman describes rating periods, uncertainty intervals and volatility and notes best performance with moderate-to-large game counts—rather than universal defaults.

Hierarchical Bayesian/state-space model: place league -> team -> unit -> player effects under partial pooling, with time-varying strength, home/venue effects, opponent, workload, age/position and availability states. Use PyMC or Stan for HMC/NUTS/MCMC, prior/posterior predictive checks and stored diagnostics; use a unified latent-strength layer but sport-specific observation models. The cited studies apply Bayesian state-space models across NFL/NHL/NBA/MLB and use shrinkage, hidden states, predictive intervals and hold-out/out-of-sample checks.

Edge/EV engine: preserve quote, timestamp, market rule and settlement. Convert American odds to implied probability using p_raw=|a|/(|a|+100), or decimal odds D using p_raw=1/D; remove overround explicitly, for example proportional normalization p_i/sum(p_i), while retaining alternative margin models. For a binary decimal-price bet with net payout D-1, EV per unit stake is p_model(D-1)-(1-p_model); publish edge p_model-p_fair, EV, posterior interval, vig method and stale-line/limit flags.

Calibration/release gates: use log loss/Brier for binary probabilities, proper distributional scores and interval coverage for score/prop distributions, reliability curves by sport/market/edge bucket, posterior predictive checks, Glicko calibration and walk-forward comparison to market/baseline. Evaluate economic output after vig, pushes/voids, limits, closing-line movement and execution; version data snapshots, posterior draws, feature code, quote, lineup state, seed and settlement rule so every edge is reproducible.

Production compute split: Kafka provides durable/replayable partitioned event streams; Flink provides keyed state, event-time computation and checkpointed exactly-once recovery; Spark Structured Streaming/Spark SQL provides batch/stream-consistent ETL, historical backfills and feature recomputation; Iceberg or Delta provides snapshots/time travel. PyMC/Stan runs asynchronous training/posterior generation, while a compiled/vectorized simulation service serves live probabilities and props.
